fields.features_heading: What a Will Intake Form Collects
fields.features_subheading: The form asks what an attorney would ask in a first meeting, and each answer lands in a record the whole firm can open.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the client's family

Asks about marriage and children first, then shows only the sections that apply. A widowed client with grown children skips the spouse and guardian pages and finishes sooner.
fields.feature_2:
A first choice and a backup for every role

Collects a backup for the executor and for each guardian, with phone, email, and relationship to the client. The attorney can call either person without asking the client twice.
fields.feature_3:
An asset list the attorney can sort

Records each account, home, vehicle, and business interest as its own row, with a rough value and how it is titled. Accounts that already name a beneficiary get their own column.
fields.feature_4:
A message when a file is ready to draft

Sends the attorney a Slack message or an email when a client submits, with a link to the answers. A client who has not submitted 3 days after the link went out gets a reminder.
fields.feature_5:
Client files in a database you own

Saves every client as one record with a status: intake, drafting, review, signing booked, signed. Records sit in a database you own, and the platform has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001.
fields.feature_6:
The form's full code in your GitHub

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then add a question your state's forms need, or connect the firm's case management system.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Sends a Will Intake Form, and When
fields.tab_content_1:
A family tree on the attorney's screen before the consult

Quarry Hill Estate Law sends each new client one link after they book. Lucinda Delacroix answers 42 questions in one sitting: her marriage, two adult children, an executor and a backup, and six assets. Attorney Celia Marwick reads the summary of her client record before their Thursday 10:00 AM consult.
fields.tab_content_2:
With a child under 18, guardian questions open

The Wexlers list three children, aged 9, 14, and 19. Because two of them are under 18, the form opens a guardian section that asks for a first choice, a backup, and whether each person has agreed to serve. Quarry Hill's paralegal sees both guardians next to the children in the client record.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each volunteer gets their clients' answers on Friday

Kettle Valley Legal Aid holds a Saturday will clinic with 24 appointments of 30 minutes each. Seniors sign up on one form that asks for their county, family, and assets, then pick a time. This week 22 slots are booked and 2 are open. On Friday at 6:00 PM, each volunteer attorney gets an email with their clients' answers.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any witness under 14 is flagged before signing day

Unless a will is written wholly in the testator's handwriting, the Texas Estates Code calls for two or more credible witnesses who are at least 14 years of age. The signing form asks Lucinda for each witness's name and age. She lists two, and her grandson Leo, 13, is flagged. The firm emails her to name another witness.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Last Will and Testament Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a last will and testament form around your intake checklist, then build it with Emergent and test it on a closed file.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what the attorney asks first
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the deciding questions up front
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for assets one row at a time
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every question your attorneys ask in a first will meeting: legal name, county, marriage, children and their ages, executor, guardians, specific gifts, and who takes the rest. Mark the questions that apply to only some clients, such as a prior marriage.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Group the questions the way a client thinks about them: family first, then the people they trust with a role, then property. Ask about marriage and children's ages at the very start, because those two answers decide which sections a client sees.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Paste your list into Emergent with the rules in plain English, such as opening the guardian section when any child is under 18. Emergent builds the form, the client table, and a view for the attorney, and any question changes with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the asset section short: the type, an estimate, and whose name is on it. Estimates are enough at intake, and the attorney can ask for statements later. Leave out full account numbers, since nobody needs them before a draft exists.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send each file to its attorney
fields.howto_step_5_des: Route a finished file to the attorney who holds the consult, by Slack message or email, and copy the paralegal who opens the client record. Decide who calls the client when an answer looks wrong, so nobody waits for the meeting to ask.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with a closed file
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill the form with the facts of a closed matter, names changed, and compare the summary with the notes the attorney took at that meeting. Any fact the summary misses points to a question you need to add or reword before a live client sees it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the link after each booking
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the link to your booking confirmation so each client answers before the consult. Have the reviewing attorney read the wording once more: the form gathers facts, and the will itself is still drafted and reviewed by the attorney.

plan.angle: The top 10 are fill-in will templates (eForms, LegalTemplates, ILRG, DoYourOwnWill), a Rocket Lawyer interview, a printed kit on Amazon, a YouTube walkthrough and two state self-help pages (Texas State Law Library, California courts). All of them serve the person writing their own will. None serves the attorney, paralegal or legal aid clinic who has to collect a client's family, executor, guardian and asset details before drafting. This page builds that intake form: questions that branch on children and marriage, an asset list, a clinic sign-up and a signing appointment that checks each witness against the Texas age rule, with every client saved as one record. It gives no legal advice and never states a signing rule outside the state its source covers.
